scope: Local synthetic Linux capacity assessment; no production application files changed and no cloud resources created.

assessment.recommended_start: 4GiB/2vCPU for the current heavy workloads;2GiB only for controlled lighter use or after image optimization.

runtime.system: Ubuntu26.04 chroot in WSL2, cgroupv2 CPU/RAM limits, private network namespace

method.peak_pss: Sum of proportional resident memory; shared pages counted proportionally
method.cgroup_memory: Includes charged file cache and kernel memory; cache ownership can differ across service restarts

findings.outcome: Twelve distinct20MPJPEGs totaling61411049bytes caused one LinuxOOMkill and HTTP500 on the2GiB simulation; the identical input passed on4GiB.
1500rows on each of3sheets exceeded540seconds of PHPexecution time in RmsQuarterlyReportDocument::cell atDOMXPathquery,line191; noOOM in that run.
Initial terminal/quarterly marker failures came from extracted-text reading order. Complete markers were verified and both workloads rerun successfully.
Initial additional archive/retrieval failures were synthetic fixture issues: a required summary field and a nondiscriminating repeated query. Corrected cases passed.

One415page terminalPDFhit the existing120second conversion timeout during the4GiB soak, withoutOOM. The separately labelled240second retry tests a deployment timeout adjustment; no application source change.

After the timeout, the oldLibreOfficebinary remained withPPID1 using837748KiBRSS, while recovery started anotherworker on a differentUNOpipeline. The oldpipeline matches the timeoutlog. LibreOfficePdfWorker::stop signals the launcher atline134; Linuxprocess-treecleanup needs review.

limitations: LocalWSLCPU and disk performance are not a DigitalOcean benchmark; cloud latency and sharedCPUvariation were not measured.
PHP8.5.4 Ubuntu backport differs from the project Composerpatch requirement; deploy with a compatible patchedPHPversion and smoke-test there.
Only remoteAIHTTPwas mocked; localGD,Poppler,LibreOffice,Node and MySQLwork were real. PaidAIlatency/usage was not tested.
Finite synthetic workloads do not prove capacity for unbounded report rows, tables, image counts, or future traffic.
Production built assets were served; frontend builds,Composerinstallation and development servers were not part of runtime memory measurements.
